newsitem.title: GERMANY: Aero Intl. wins 12 regional aircraft contracts.
newsitem.headline: Aero Intl. wins 12 regional aircraft contracts.

text.p: European aircraft manufacturer Aero International (Regional) said it has won a string of orders for new and used aircraft for delivery in 1997.
The European consortium said it already has 12 contracts from around the world for nine new and 11 used aircraft for 1997.
AI(R) aircraft now have a 49 percent share of the market for 40 to 70-seat turboprops and 21 percent of the regional jet aircraft market, a statement said.
Among the contracts, Dutch airline Air Exel Commuter has ordered three second-hand ATR 42-300 aircraft with the first delivery due in March 1997.
The carrier, a partner of KLM Royal Dutch Airlines, will operate the aircraft between Maastricht and Amsterdam, and between Eindhoven, London Heathrow and Paris Charles de Gaulle.
Romanian carrier Tarom plans to operate two renovated ATR 42 aircraft on routes from Bucharest to Sofia, Kiev, Budapest and Saloniki.
Air Lithuania has ordered a new ATR 42-300 and taken an option for other aircraft as part of a fleet renewal programme.
Air Sicilia and French carrier Regional Airlines have ordered second-hand ATR 42s, and a new ATR 72-210A will be delivered to Air Guadeloupe.
Four South American airlines, Total in Brazil, Santa Barbara and IAACA in Venezuela and Mayan World Airlines in Guatemala have ordered a total of seven aircraft.
In Asia, Air Tahiti has ordered three ATR 72-210A and Bangkok Airways has ordered a seventh ATR 42. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
